summary: Resume synchronization after the last propagated block expires during an upstream outage
details: When a propagated block leaves the thirty-minute validation queue, retain its download target in the connected peer's head metadata using a known local or advertised parent TD. This allows recovery even when the peer previously advertised only a parent already present locally.
Release block bodies and peer queue quotas on expiry, coalesce sync wakeups, and advance peer hints atomically so delayed parent gossip cannot overwrite the recovery target.

Re-download and validate the block through the existing downloader, preserving external-state retry budgets, cooldown, permanent local error handling and consensus verification. No new block, manual reconnection or recovery restart is required for a temporary upstream lag.
